notes: Highly irregular verb; essential auxiliary for perfect tense with motion/state-change verbs. Irregular in all forms.

examples.german: Ich fahre jeden Tag zur Arbeit.
examples.english: I drive to work every day.

examples.german: Er wird morgen mit dem Zug fahren.
examples.english: He will travel by train tomorrow.

notes: Vowel change a → ä in 2nd and 3rd person singular present. Takes 'sein' as auxiliary because it expresses directed motion.
Key auxiliary for perfect tense with most transitive verbs. Irregular in 2nd/3rd singular present.

examples.english: We will go for a walk.

notes: Takes 'sein' as auxiliary. Simple past 'ging' is suppletive. Very common in daily speech.
Takes 'sein' as auxiliary. Frequently used with prefixes: ankommen, vorkommen, bekommen.

examples.german: Was wirst du heute Abend machen?

notes: Regular weak verb. One of the most common verbs in German. Used in many fixed expressions.
Regular weak verb. Often followed by a subordinate clause with 'dass'. Distinguish from 'erzählen' (to narrate) and 'sprechen' (to speak).

examples.english: We will see each other soon.

notes: Vowel change e → ie in 2nd/3rd singular present. Strong verb with irregular simple past 'sah'.

examples.german: Hast du gewusst, dass er kommt?
examples.english: Did you know he was coming?

notes: Preterite-present verb: singular present looks like a past tense form. Different from 'kennen' (to know a person/place).

examples.english: Will you get to know him?

notes: Mixed verb: weak past tense with vowel change (kennen → kannte). Distinct from 'wissen' (factual knowledge).

examples.german: Sie hat ihm die Schlüssel gegeben.
Wirst du mir deine Nummer geben?
examples.english: Will you give me your number?

notes: Vowel change e → i in 2nd/3rd singular present. Also used impersonally: 'es gibt' = there is/are.

examples.german: Er nahm das Buch vom Regal.
examples.english: He took the book from the shelf.

notes: Strong vowel change: nehm- → nimm- in singular present. Simple past 'nahm' is highly irregular.

examples.english: He is standing at the door.

examples.german: Ich stand lange in der Schlange.
examples.english: I stood in line for a long time.

examples.german: Sie wird vor dem Gebäude stehen.
examples.english: She will stand in front of the building.

notes: In southern Germany and Austria, 'sein' may be used as auxiliary instead of 'haben'.

examples.german: Das Buch liegt auf dem Tisch.
examples.english: The book is lying on the table.
Munich has been located in Bavaria.

examples.german: Die Unterlagen werden auf deinem Schreibtisch liegen.
examples.english: The documents will be on your desk.

notes: Distinguishes from 'legen' (to lay/place). Regional variation with 'sein' as auxiliary in south Germany/Austria.

examples.english: She is sitting at the window.
I will sit in the front.

notes: Distinguishes from 'setzen' (to set/place). Uses 'sein' as auxiliary in southern German dialects.

examples.english: She will run in the marathon.

notes: Vowel change a → ä in 2nd/3rd singular present. Takes 'sein' for directed motion. Can also mean 'to walk' in everyday speech.

examples.german: Wir haben über das Problem gesprochen.
Ich werde mit dem Chef sprechen.
examples.english: I will speak with the boss.

notes: Vowel change e → i in 2nd/3rd singular present. Used with 'mit' for conversations and 'über' for topics.
Strong verb with diphthong change ei → ie in simple past. Very common in academic and professional contexts.
Vowel change e → ie in 2nd/3rd singular present (liest). Note: du liest and er liest look identical.

examples.german: Was wirst du zum Frühstück essen?
examples.english: What will you eat for breakfast?

notes: Vowel change e → i in 2nd/3rd singular (isst). Note: du isst and er isst are identical. Distinguish from 'fressen' (eating by animals).

examples.english: He drank a glass of water.

notes: Strong verb with vowel change i → a → u (trinken, trank, getrunken). Common in daily conversation.

examples.english: I slept for a long time.
I will go to sleep early.

notes: Vowel change a → ä in 2nd/3rd singular present. Strong verb class with diphthong in simple past 'schlief'.

examples.german: Ich arbeite von neun bis fünf.
examples.english: I work from nine to five.

examples.german: Er wird nächste Woche nicht arbeiten.
examples.english: He will not work next week.

notes: Regular weak verb, but adds -e- before -t endings (arbeitest, arbeitet, arbeitete) for pronunciation. Very frequent in everyday German.
Regular weak verb. Opposite: 'verkaufen' (to sell). Frequently used with 'ein-kaufen' (to go shopping).

examples.english: The children are playing in the garden.
She will perform in the theatre.

notes: Regular weak verb. Used for sports, instruments, and games. Musical instruments use 'Klavier/Geige spielen' (no article).
Vowel change e → i in 2nd/3rd singular present. Governs dative case: 'jemandem helfen'.
Regular weak verb. Distinct from 'studieren' (to study at university). Used for skill acquisition and studying.
Mixed verb: consonant change (denken → dachte). Used with 'an + accusative' to mean 'to think of/about someone'.
Regular weak verb. Use 'nach' for asking about something: 'nach dem Weg fragen'. Reflexive: 'sich fragen' = to wonder.
Regular weak verb with -e- insertion (antwortest, antwortet). Governs dative: 'jemandem antworten'. 'auf + accusative' for the subject of response.

examples.english: He used to live in Munich.

examples.german: Sie hat lange in Wien gewohnt.
examples.english: She lived in Vienna for a long time.

examples.german: Wir werden in der Stadt wohnen.
examples.english: We will live in the city.

notes: Regular weak verb. Specifically means to reside (ongoing). Distinguished from 'leben' (to live/be alive). Used with 'in + dative'.

examples.german: Ich habe lange in Japan gelebt.
examples.english: I lived in Japan for a long time.

notes: Regular weak verb. Has existential meaning. Can also mean 'to reside' informally, like 'wohnen'.

englishMeaning: to be called / to be named

examples.english: That used to be called something else.

notes: Governs nominative. Du heißt and er heißt are identical. Also used impersonally: 'Es heißt, dass...' (It is said that...).
Inseparable prefix 'ver-'. No 'ge-' in past participle prefix. Reflexive: 'sich verstehen' = to get along with someone.
Regular weak verb. In informal German, often used as modal verb: 'Du brauchst nicht zu kommen' (You don't need to come). 'gebraucht' also means 'used/second-hand'.
Strong verb with vowel change i → a → u. Also used to express opinion: 'Ich finde das gut' (I think that's good).

examples.german: Ich werde dich nach Hause bringen.

notes: Mixed verb with consonant change: bringen → brachte. Both a direct object (accusative) and indirect object (dative) possible.

examples.english: I want to become a doctor.

notes: Modal verb: 1st and 3rd singular present have no ending (ich will, er will). Followed by infinitive without 'zu'.

examples.english: Were you able to do that?
She will be able to do it.

notes: Modal verb: 1st and 3rd singular without ending (ich kann, er kann). Expresses ability or possibility. Konjunktiv II 'könnte' = could.

examples.english: I have to get up early.
He had to do the task.
She had to wait for a long time.
We will have to be on time.

notes: Modal verb. 1st/3rd singular: muss. Expresses necessity. 'müsste' (Konjunktiv II) = should/ought to (polite). Perfect with double infinitive: 'hat warten müssen'.

examples.english: He wasn't allowed to go out.
She wasn't allowed to do that.
Will you be allowed to do that?

notes: Modal verb expressing permission. 1st/3rd singular: darf. Konjunktiv II 'dürfte' = probably/might (epistemic use).

examples.english: He was supposed to arrive at eight.
He wasn't supposed to do that.
What is that supposed to mean?

notes: Modal verb expressing expectation or external obligation. Konjunktiv II 'sollte' = should. 1st/3rd singular: soll.
Konjunktiv II 'möchte' is used as a polite form for 'would like to'. Extremely common in shops and restaurants.

examples.german: Das Geschäft hat um neun geöffnet.

notes: Regular weak verb with -e- insertion. Synonym 'aufmachen' (separable) is more colloquial.

examples.german: Das Museum hat um 18 Uhr geschlossen.

notes: Strong verb: schließt in 2nd/3rd person singular (no additional -t). Past tense 'schloss' with double-s rule applies.

examples.english: He was looking for a job.
We searched for a long time.
She will look for an apartment.

notes: Regular weak verb. Directly takes an accusative object (no preposition needed), unlike English 'look for'.
Inseparable prefix 'be-'. Strong vowel change in simple past and past participle. Synonym: 'anfangen' (separable, more colloquial).

examples.german: Er hörte mit dem Rauchen auf.

notes: Separable verb: prefix 'auf-' splits to end of clause in main clauses. 'ge-' inserted between prefix and stem in past participle.

examples.german: Ich fange mit der Arbeit an.

notes: Separable strong verb. Vowel change a → ä in 2nd/3rd singular present. More colloquial than 'beginnen'. Followed by 'zu + infinitive'.

examples.german: Ich stehe um sieben Uhr auf.
examples.english: I get up at seven o'clock.

notes: Separable verb with 'sein' as auxiliary. Strong verb base 'stehen'. Common in daily routine descriptions.

examples.german: Ich bin vor dem Film eingeschlafen.
examples.english: I fell asleep before the film.

notes: Separable, takes 'sein'. State change: going from awake to asleep. Opposite: aufwachen (to wake up).

examples.english: He woke up from the noise.

examples.german: Sie ist mitten in der Nacht aufgewacht.
examples.english: She woke up in the middle of the night.

notes: Separable, takes 'sein' (state change). Distinguished from 'aufwecken' (to wake someone else up).
Inseparable prefix 'be-'. No 'ge-' in past participle. Also used for attending institutions: 'die Schule besuchen' (to attend school).
Inseparable 'ver-'. Past participle 'vergessen' looks like infinitive. e → i in 2nd/3rd singular (vergisst).

examples.german: Er erinnerte mich an das Meeting.
examples.english: He reminded me of the meeting.

examples.german: Sie hat sich an alles erinnert.

notes: Two uses: 'jemanden an etwas erinnern' (to remind someone of something) and 'sich an etwas erinnern' (to remember something, reflexive).
Inseparable 'be-'. Also 'zahlen' (to pay) without prefix. 'bezahlen' usually takes a direct object; 'zahlen' often used intransitively.
Regular weak verb. Also means 'to boil' (for liquids). 'das Wasser kocht' = the water is boiling.
Regular weak verb. Common in household and hygiene contexts. 'sich die Zähne putzen' (reflexive with dative for body parts).

examples.german: Hast du dir die Hände gewaschen?

notes: Vowel change a → ä in 2nd/3rd singular present. Reflexive 'sich waschen' = to wash oneself. Body parts take dative with reflexive.

examples.english: They are building a new house.

examples.german: Die Stadt hat ein Stadion gebaut.

notes: Regular weak verb. Frequently used in construction and architecture contexts. 'auf etwas bauen' = to rely on something.

examples.english: The leaf falls from the tree.

notes: Vowel change a → ä in 2nd/3rd singular. Takes 'sein'. Note: 'gefallen' also means 'to please' (Das gefällt mir = I like that).

examples.german: Wir sind in den Bus gestiegen.

notes: Takes 'sein'. Used for climbing, rising prices, and boarding vehicles. Diphthong ei → ie in simple past.
Takes 'sein' for directed motion. Strong verb with vowel change ie → o in simple past.

examples.german: Sie ist über den See geschwommen.

notes: Takes 'sein' for directed motion. Uses 'haben' when expressing general activity without direction.

examples.english: They are dancing at the party.
She will dance at the concert.

notes: Regular weak verb. When expressing directed motion while dancing, takes 'sein': 'Er ist in den Saal getanzt'.
Strong verb with vowel gradation i → a → u. Belongs to the same ablaut class as trinken, beginnen.

examples.english: She will listen to the radio.

notes: Regular weak verb. Distinguish between hearing (passive: ich höre) and listening (active: ich höre zu / zuhören).
Regular weak verb. Commonly used reflexively: 'sich fühlen' + adjective for emotional/physical states. Also transitive: 'etwas fühlen' (to feel something).
Regular weak verb. Followed by 'dass' clause or 'auf + accusative' (to hope for something).
Regular weak verb. 'jemandem glauben' (dative) = to believe a person. 'an + accusative' = to believe in something. 'dass' clause for content.

examples.german: Sie hat mir die Fotos gezeigt.
Wir werden euch das Ergebnis zeigen.
examples.english: We will show you the result.

notes: Regular weak verb. Takes two objects: accusative (thing shown) + dative (person). 'auf + accusative' = to point to something.

examples.english: Can you explain that to me?

notes: Inseparable prefix 'er-'. No 'ge-' prefix in past participle. Used in both academic and everyday contexts.

examples.english: I will tell you about it.

notes: Inseparable prefix. Use 'von + dative' to narrate about something. More narrative than 'sagen'; implies telling a longer story.
Inseparable prefix 'ver-'. Strong vowel change ie → o. Past participle 'verloren' also used in expression 'verloren gehen' (to get lost).
Strong vowel change i → a → o. Note: 'ge-' here is the inseparable prefix (from Old High German origin), not the past participle marker.

examples.german: Die Kinder rechnen in der Schule.
examples.english: The children do arithmetic at school.

notes: Regular weak verb with -e- insertion. 'mit etwas rechnen' = to expect/count on something. Common in school and business.

examples.german: Ich treffe mich heute mit ihr.
Wir haben uns im Café getroffen.

notes: Vowel change e → i in 2nd/3rd singular present. Reflexive 'sich treffen' = to meet each other. Also used in sports for hitting a target.
Regular weak verb with -e- insertion. Followed by 'auf + accusative' (to wait for something/someone).
Regular weak verb taking 'sein' for directed motion. 'durch + accusative' = through; 'nach + city/country' = to a destination.

examples.german: Der Zug kommt um 15 Uhr an.

notes: Separable verb taking 'sein'. 'es kommt auf + accusative an' = it depends on. Very common in travel and scheduling contexts.

examples.german: Der Bus fährt um 9 Uhr ab.

examples.english: We will set off early tomorrow.

notes: Separable, takes 'sein'. Contrast with 'ankommen' (to arrive). Very common in public transport contexts.

examples.english: You need to change trains in Frankfurt.
You will change trains in Hamburg.

notes: Separable, takes 'sein'. Specifically used for changing between trains, buses, etc. Part of transport vocabulary.

examples.german: Ich lade dich zur Party ein.
examples.english: I'm inviting you to the party.

examples.german: Ich werde dich zum Essen einladen.
examples.english: I will invite you for dinner.

notes: Separable, strong. Unusual: 2nd person singular present is 'du lädst' (vowel change a → ä). 'zu etwas einladen' = to invite to something.
Separable. Two key meanings: 'jemanden vorstellen' = to introduce someone; 'sich etwas vorstellen' = to imagine something.

examples.german: Er ruhte sich nach dem Sport aus.
Sie wird sich am Wochenende ausruhen.
examples.english: She will rest on the weekend.

notes: Separable, almost always used reflexively: 'sich ausruhen'. Adjective 'ausgeruht' (well-rested) is very common.

examples.german: Sie wird sich nach der Arbeit umziehen.
examples.english: She will change clothes after work.

notes: Separable, strong. Takes 'sein' for relocation; takes 'haben' in reflexive 'sich umziehen' (to change clothes). Different auxiliaries!
Separable, strong. Diphthong change u → ie in simple past. Very common in daily communication.

examples.german: Sie hat mich vom Bahnhof abgeholt.
examples.english: She picked me up from the station.

notes: Separable, regular. Very common in everyday German for collecting people or items.
Separable strong verb (stem from 'nehmen'). Vowel change in singular present (nimmt mit). Used when taking something along on a journey.
Separable verb (zurück- + kommen), takes 'sein'. Very frequent in everyday speech.

examples.german: Das Konzert findet im Park statt.
examples.english: The concert takes place in the park.

examples.german: Die Konferenz fand letztes Jahr statt.
examples.english: The conference took place last year.

examples.german: Das Festival wird im Sommer stattfinden.
examples.english: The festival will take place in summer.

notes: Separable strong verb. Always used without a personal subject (no reflexive). Common in formal contexts and event planning.

examples.german: Er passte auf die Kinder auf.

examples.english: You will need to be careful.

notes: Separable, regular. 'auf + accusative aufpassen' = to look after someone/something. Common warning command: 'Pass auf!'

examples.english: He thought for a long time.

examples.german: Sie wird es sich noch nachdenken.
examples.english: She will think about it some more.

notes: Separable mixed verb (stem from 'denken': dachte). Used with 'über + accusative' for the topic of reflection.

examples.english: I have to tidy up my room.

examples.german: Wir werden nach der Party aufräumen.
examples.english: We will clean up after the party.

notes: Separable, regular. Adjective 'aufgeräumt' also means 'tidy' or 'in a good mood'. Common in household contexts.

englishMeaning: to stay overnight / spend the night

examples.english: We are staying overnight in the hotel.
I spent the night in Berlin.
She will spend the night in a tent.

notes: Inseparable prefix 'über-'. Regular weak verb. Very common in travel and tourism vocabulary.
Inseparable 'be-'. Used for ordering food, online shopping, and booking services.

examples.english: I would like to reserve a table.

notes: Regular weak verb from French. Common in restaurants, hotels, and transport. 'Haben Sie reserviert?' is a standard question.

examples.german: Ich entscheide mich für das Blaue.
examples.english: I decide on the blue one.

notes: Inseparable 'ent-'. Strong diphthong change ei → ie. Reflexive 'sich entscheiden für/gegen' = to decide for/against something.

examples.english: The house belonged to his grandmother.

notes: Inseparable 'ge-'. Governs dative: 'jemandem gehören'. Also used: 'zu etwas gehören' (to be part of something).

examples.german: Ein Unfall passierte auf der Autobahn.
examples.english: An accident happened on the motorway.

examples.german: Das ist mir noch nie passiert.
examples.english: That has never happened to me before.

notes: Takes 'sein' for the meaning 'to happen'. Takes 'haben' when meaning 'to pass (a place)'. Governs dative for the affected person: 'mir passiert'.
